title: Care Management Bulletin: Discharge Sessions and Expired Prior Authorization Units
content:
**Care Management coordination bulletin — Prior Authorization units kept for discharge sessions**

**Rule.** The discharge-session hold-back of an expiry release of a Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization approval looks at the member's active care management episode and at the care-transition follow-ups its care team recorded within the two months before the day the release is booked:

- where the active episode is Complex Case Management or Health Home Services and at least one such follow-up is recorded, 2 units are held back for the program's discharge sessions;
- where the active episode is of any other care management tier and at least one such follow-up is recorded, 1 unit is held back;
- where there is no active episode or no such follow-up, nothing is held back for discharge sessions.

The hold-back is a whole number of units, taken once from the units the ended approval left unused; the units released are never below zero.

**Records read.** The member's Care Management episode that is active on the booking day (its tier), and the care-transition follow-up activities its care team recorded with an activity date inside the two months before the booking day. Other kinds of care activity, such as contacts or care plan updates, do not count.

### Truth table

| Active Care Management episode | Care-transition follow-up in the two months before the booking day | Units held back |
|---|---|---|
| Complex Case Management or Health Home Services | At least 1 | 2 |
| Complex Case Management or Health Home Services | None | 0 |
| Any other tier (for example Care Coordination Level 1 or Maternal Care Management) | At least 1 | 1 |
| Any other tier | None | 0 |
| No active episode | Any | 0 |

### Hypothetical cases, for illustration only

- Active Health Home Services episode, one care-transition follow-up recorded five weeks before the booking day: **2 units**.
- Active Care Coordination Level 2 episode, two follow-ups in the window: **1 unit** (the count of follow-ups above one does not raise it).
- Active Complex Case Management episode whose last follow-up was recorded four months before: **nothing**.
